newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia police chief "ready to fight".
newsitem.headline: Cambodia police chief "ready to fight".

text.p: Cambodian national police chief Hok Lundy on Wednesday accused one of the country's co-premiers of attacking his home and said he was ready to fight.
He said his bodyguards had been attacked overnight by guards of co-premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh which led to an hour-long exchange of gun and mortar fire.
Hok Lundy blamed Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party for the fighting. "I have increased my bodyguards for my safety but we're not afraid if FUNCINPEC wants to continue fighting," he said.

Hok Lundy is a member of rival co-Premier Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party. The police chief, surrounded by his bodyguards, told a news conference outside his home that the house had been attacked by 40 armed men sent by FUNCINPEC Secretary of State for the Interior Ho Sok.
Two of the FUNCINPEC men were killed he said. He did not report any deaths among his own bodyguards.
He said Hun Sen had asked him to "not to make the situation tense." Cambodia's capital was calm on Wednesday morning after the fighting between 10.30 p.m. (1530 GMT) and midnight (1700 GMT).
